The operators define a stochastic framework for modeling football team performance using maximum likelihood estimation of attack and defense parameters. These parameters are derived from historical goal data and represent latent strengths within a Poisson process model. The dual nature of these parameters—attack and defense—implies an inverse relationship: higher attack implies lower defensive vulnerability. Failure modes arise when data is sparse or when teams exhibit non-stationary behavior, invalidating the assumption of fixed parameters. The model assumes independence among matches and stationarity of team abilities, which may not hold during periods of significant roster changes or tactical shifts. The use of standard errors provides uncertainty quantification, essential for Bayesian inference in GSI and for probabilistic reasoning in GSE.
